stage_a.note: smiles broadly while confidently stating his sales figures and growth
energetic and engaged delivery when announcing his five million dollar projection
friendly opening greeting, though balanced with a confrontational stance later

venture.description: Premium wine sold by the glass in patented, single-serve, sealed containers.
venture.note: Sells to consumers via large retailers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Greets the panel playfully upon his return to the tank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces himself, states his ask, recaps his massive sales growth since his last appearance, and addresses Kevin directly.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Challenges the founder's decision to bottle the wine himself rather than licensing the technology to the entire industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Deflects the licensing question by asking Kevin to recall the specific offer he walked away from last time.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reminds the founder that the offer was his, for six hundred thousand dollars for fifty-one percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asserts that the previous offer was a great deal and that the founder made a mistake by rejecting it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Jokes about what the founder is drinking to be brave enough to return to the tank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokes back that he does not remember them being gentle during his first appearance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Responds to the challenge by asserting that the brand and patents are now much more valuable than before.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Recalls calling him a dead man walking and asks if his current success is real or a ghost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Deflects the question by revealing a poster of a custom wine bottle named Dead Man Walking dedicated to Kevin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Proposes licensing the technology to the largest players to quadruple his net worth, reiterating his original offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks Kevin to clarify if he is offering the exact same deal as the previous season.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Confirms that he is returning to his original offer because it is the right thing to do.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Recalls that the founder passed out wine samples last time and asks him to do it again.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands out the wine samples to the panel, pointing out how easy it is to serve.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Remarks that he is waiting for the good stuff while receiving his sample.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Declares he is out because he wasn't interested last time and just wants to be entertained.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Expresses strong interest in partnering on the packaging side of the business rather than the winery side.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: States discomfort with the six million dollar valuation and asks if the founder is negotiable on the equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that he is there to negotiate but insists the panel take his expertise and information seriously.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Presses the founder on what it will take to make a deal happen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains his valuation by stating that most national brands sell for two and a half to three times gross value.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Counters the valuation argument by stating the founder's brand is not yet at that national level.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Exits the deal, stating she has the same visceral negative reaction to him as during his first pitch.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks the founder to move the needle on the valuation so the panel can respond with an offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Acknowledges their interest and suggests that if they can work on the valuation, a deal might be possible.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Makes a new offer, valuing the company at exactly what he believes it is worth right now.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Clarifies the implied valuation of Kevin's new offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Confirms that the valuation he offered is exactly what the company is worth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Pitches his offer by promising to eventually convince the founder to license the technology globally for massive profit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the founder has anyone he can call before making a decision, seeking a moment alone with the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms he has someone to call and leaves the room.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Suggests to the other investors that they combine forces to offer more money for a larger total equity stake.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks the founder who he called while he was out of the room.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reveals he called Jim Koch, the founder of Samuel Adams, who has been instrumental in advising him.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what advice the founder received during the phone call.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that the advisor wanted to ensure any new partner shares the vision and understands the possibilities.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the advisor is an investor or equity owner in the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies that the advisor does not hold any equity in the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Questions why the advisor does not simply provide the funding needed for the extra line.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that the best advice comes from someone who is not financially invested in the company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Brings the conversation back to the negotiation by asking what the advisor recommended regarding Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters the standing offer, proposing a lower equity stake in exchange for partnering with established investors.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Confirms that the founder has just made his counter offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Immediately rejects the founder's counter offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks Mark to explain why he is not interested in the counter offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Explains the value the sharks bring and makes a combined offer on behalf of himself, Robert, and Kevin.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Highlights that the combined offer provides twice the capital the founder originally asked for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees with the logic of more skin in the game and asks if it guarantees distribution in the Mavericks stadium.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Clarifies he cannot guarantee the stadium but offers distribution in his Landmark theaters.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Urges the founder to stop talking himself out of a sale and to make a decision.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Warns the founder not to repeat his past mistake of walking away from a deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Emphasizes the unique opportunity of the combined offer and confirms the three participating investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Expresses concern about Kevin potentially wanting to split up the company later.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Reassures the founder that he and Mark will keep Kevin in line, praising the concept's growth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Demands that the founder make a decision right now.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States his desire to partner but questions the value added to justify giving up thirty percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells the founder he simply has to decide.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Refuses to sell the panel's value back to the founder, insisting the offer is fair and demanding a decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Silently opens the custom wine bottle while contemplating the offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reiterates the thirty percent equity stake condition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Looks at the bottle and remarks on the discrepancy between its theoretical value and the offered price.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells the founder he is not thinking clearly about the deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Interrupts Kevin, interpreting the founder's actions as an acceptance of the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Offers to drink the wine with the founder in celebration of the deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Presses the founder for his final answer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Rejects the combined offer and walks away from the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reacts with visible frustration to the rejection.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Exits angrily, accusing the founder of playing games and creating drama instead of negotiating.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Follows Mark's lead and formally exits the deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Jokes about whether Kevin and Robert will still split the deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Reiterates her exit, telling the founder he just came to waste their time.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Offers a sarcastic toast as the founder leaves the tank.

decisions.note: Wants to license the technology to the largest players to quadruple net worth.
Was not interested last time and is just watching for entertainment.
Has the same visceral negative reaction to the founder as during his first pitch.
Puts an offer out because that is exactly what he believes the company is worth.
Adviser recommended paying additionally above the ask for a partner like Mark Cuban.
Combined offer from Mark, Robert, and Kevin to provide significant support and skin in the game.
Does not see enough value added by the sharks to justify the discounted valuation.
Feels the founder is playing games and creating drama instead of negotiating.
Follows Mark out after the founder rejects the combined offer.

record.notes: An interview segment with Jim Koch on the phone is edited into the middle of the pitch while the founder is out of the room.
